subject: Clarify chain-of-custody, EU residency & deletion timeline for post-incident logs
messages:
From: security@finbank.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: legal@finbank.com
Date: 2026-12-10T14:15:00+00:00
Subject: Request: post-incident retention & chain-of-custody for logs

Hi Kimberly,

Following the incident we discussed this morning, FinBank needs confirmation on the following points for our internal audit:
- Exact retention window for application logs and request traces generated during the incident window (UTC 2026-12-08 22:00 - 2026-12-09 03:00).
- Where are copies stored (primary region, replicated regions, snapshots/backups)?
- Do you keep immutable forensic exports or object-locked buckets?
- Chain-of-custody steps you follow for producing a forensic export (hashing, signature, who signs off).
- Deletion workflow: what triggers deletion, who authorizes, and whether deletion cascades to backups/third-party indexes.

We also need a timestamped export and manifest we can submit to our legal team. Please advise next steps and expected SLA for providing the artifacts.

Thanks,
Alex Moretti
Head of Security Operations, FinBank
security@finbank.com

--
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: security@finbank.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-10T16:05:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Request: post-incident retention & chain-of-custody for logs

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear ask. High level answers below; Ill attach the initial forensic export and manifest for your team to intake. Marissa, Vivek, Karthik have been looped for legal/SRE/compliance details.

Summary (short):
- Export delivered: attached forensic-export-20261210.zip (contains hashed log bundles + s3-manifest).
- Primary storage: EU-west region (Frankfurt) - all active logs and indexes for this customer are in the EU region.
- Replication: we do not mirror customer request logs outside EU by default. Operational snapshots for disaster recovery are kept in EU, object-locked where requested.
- Chain-of-custody: we create a time-stamped export, compute SHA256 manifest, store the manifest in a write-once audit bucket, and record the action in the audit log with the operator's user id.
- Retention: default host retention is 90 days. For incidents we mark the export with an incident hold; retention is extended until written release from FinBank or a legal hold resolution.
- Deletion workflow: explicit delete requests are gated by two approvers (SRE lead + Legal). Deletion includes: indexes, raw blobs, and any customer-facing caches; we run a cascading job that also flags backups for removal — but we do not auto-delete an export under legal hold.

Attachments: forensic-export-20261210.zip (bundle), s3-manifest-logs-20261211.csv (manifest listing object keys, sizes, sha256).

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa and FinBank legal confirm hold window (suggest: at least 180 days for initial investigation).
2) Vivek to provide exact object-lock configuration and proof of geographic residency for the exported objects.
3) I will schedule a short 30-min review with your SecOps to walk through the manifest and chain-of-custody record — available tomorrow 09:00-11:00 UTC.

Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Security Ops
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: forensic-export-20261210.zip (2.1MB, .zip)]

Alex / Kimberly — quick legal note:

- If FinBank requires data to be held >1 year, we need to sign the Data Transfer Addendum (DTA) to document responsibilities for cross-border access and extended retention.
- Any export we deliver will include a notarized manifest (signed by a Redwood officer) if FinBank plans to use the artifact in regulatory filings. Please tell us if youll need that.

Action items for FinBank legal: review the DocuSign DTA link (I can send the template) and confirm hold duration.

Best,

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, security@finbank.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-11T08:35:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Request: post-incident retention & chain-of-custody for logs

Hi all — technical details from SRE side:
- For this export we created an immutable bucket in eu-west-1 with object lock (governance mode) and a 1-year retention period; however we will not auto-delete while FinBank or Redwood legal has an active hold flag.
- Export process:
  1) Snapshot request logs from primary index (read-only snapshot).
  2) Bundle per-hour tar files, compute SHA256 per file, then compute SHA256 over manifest.
  3) Upload tar files + manifest to the immutable bucket and write the manifest hash to the audit ledger.
  4) Capture operator identity and timestamp in the export record (audit events attached).
- Replication: no cross-border replication for these keys; backups and DR snapshots are retained in eu-west only for this tenant.
- Backups: daily backups are incremental; we have a retention lifecycle for backups that is separate from forensic exports. Backup objects are not in the immutable export bucket by default, but when a legal hold is requested we create a tagged snapshot and preserve it.

Attached is the S3 manifest (s3-manifest-logs-20261211.csv) listing object keys and the SHA256 column. I can also provide the audit ledger entries for the export if FinBank wants a signed ledger extract.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: s3-manifest-logs-20261211.csv]

--
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: security@finbank.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-11T13:20:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Request: post-incident retention & chain-of-custody for logs

Adding compliance/residency notes:
- Residency: for FinBank we ensure indexes and raw logs are only searchable and stored in eu-west by tenant configuration. Any processing that needs global services is done using pseudonymized IDs; no raw request payloads are transferred out.
- Deletion cascade: our standard deletion job runs in three phases — mark, verify removal from indexes, erase blobs. The script that erases blobs (erase-blobs-v2) is run manually under two-approver flow when not under hold.
- Third-party indexes: if FinBank allowed any external integrations (e.g., CloudCorp analytics), we need explicit confirmation that those third parties have removed copies. We will not delete our primary artifacts until we receive affirmation from authorized external parties or a joint attestation.
- Suggested timeline:
  • Initial hold: 180 days (investigation)
  • Extended hold: escalate to Legal if >365 days required

Ill update the compliance ticket SEC-3218 with the object keys and the proposed deletion workflow (linked above).

Karthik Iyer
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
